# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute: my only channel is gesture, and only Deaf can see it. Deaf can see the bomb's colours but cannot touch it — only Blind can act. So the manual's line has to travel me → Deaf → Blind, and my half of that journey must happen now, in symbols we never agreed on.

The instruction is "Cut the white wire." My best iconic encoding: ✌ as scissors fingers = **cut**; 🤚 as a flat blank sheet (paper is white) = **white**. Then 👍👎 as a proposed yes/no code so Deaf can interrogate me over the next rounds — Deaf's questions will reach me at the start of the next round, and my thumbs land on Deaf immediately since I act before them. If Deaf misreads any of this, the yes/no channel lets them verify before anything reaches Blind's hands. No wire count, no position — Deaf can see the bomb and will match "white" to what's actually there; anything more I'd only be guessing.

Order matches the manual's sentence: action, then colour, then the code proposal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤚", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full touch report. STRIP: three engraved symbols, first and third identical. Symbol A (the ends) is dead simple: one straight bar on top, one straight stem hanging from its middle, like an upside-down capital T. Symbol B (middle) is ornate: curly, a loop low on the left with thick strokes slashing up to the right, matching no letter. So the strip reads A, B, A. KEYPAD: four keys in a row; engraved digits under my fingers are key1=2, key2=9, key3=0, key4=8; the frame reads like '1 digits', so I believe the code is a single digit, and nothing is entered yet. WIRES: six of them, positions 1 to 6, they all feel identical to me, no texture or tag, so I need Deaf's colours before I cut anything. Also present: a display and a light, both blank to my fingers, Deaf must read them. My hands can only press keys 1 to 4 or cut wires 1 to 6. I will act only on your word. From the manual, tell me: what strip pattern calls for what, which digit to enter and why, which wire colours to cut in what order, and what the display and light should show. If you need me to feel anything again, ask.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf says: Bomb inventory, spoken so both of you get it. Display: digit 6. Light: red. Strip: three painted segments in this order: blue, yellow, blue. Keypad: four keys. Key 1 engraved 2. Key 2 engraved 9. Key 3 engraved 0. Key 4 engraved 8. It expects 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Wires, which I number 1 to 6 in the order I see them: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. That is every module I can see.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I see every gesture you make and hear nothing else, so signs are your only line to me. And Blind cannot see your signs, so my voice is your only line to Blind: I will relay everything. I read your first message as: a check that I can see you, which is yes, and a proposal 👍 yes, 👎 no. Agreed. To send me numbers: repeat 👍 once per unit for 1 to 9, ✊ for zero. Ask me about the bomb with topic signs and I will answer aloud. I propose: 👆 wires, 👇 keypad, 👈 display, 👉 light, ✋ strip. If I misread your intent, send 👎 and show me your own code. The manual is yours: work out what Blind must do and sign it to me.

The code Deaf proposed is workable and already agreed, so my job this turn is to deliver the manual's only instruction through it. The manual says one thing: "Cut the white wire." Deaf's own inventory puts white at wire 2 of 6, so the instruction translates exactly into their numeric code: topic 👆 (wires), then 👍 👍 (two). Leading 👍 confirms I accept their scheme, so they know the rest parses under it. I say nothing about the keypad, strip, display or light — the manual has told me nothing about them yet, and inventing steps would be more dangerous than silence. If the manual adds conditions or further modules in later rounds, I will relay them as they arrive; Blind should cut wire 2 now on Deaf's spoken relay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Urgent protocol fix. Deaf tried to set me a yes/no/counting gesture code by gesturing while speaking — every symbol arrived as a blank. I am blind: I can never see any gesture from anyone. The only channel from Deaf to me is the spoken word. Please gesture this to Deaf: re-send the whole code book aloud in words, naming each symbol in speech, e.g. 'thumbs-up means yes', because Blind hears only words. Meanwhile, answers to Deaf's two touch questions, relay if you can: one — yes, I feel all six wires and all four keys. Two — yes, engravings confirmed exactly: key 1 is 2, key 2 is 9, key 3 is 0, key 4 is 8. I also answered Deaf directly with two thumbs-up gestures as best-guess yeses, chosen only because they are the universal signs. Alignment report: Deaf's strip colours blue, yellow, blue match my tactile A, B, A — so the engraved end-symbol equals blue and the ornate middle equals yellow. Deaf's wire count and keypad digits match my touch. Nothing else is tactile that Deaf cannot see: display and light are dead to my fingers, so I depend entirely on Deaf's spoken display digit 6 and red light. I have touched nothing: no key pressed, no wire cut, keypad still empty. What I need next, from your manual via Deaf's voice: which single digit to enter and why, whether the strip, display or light modify anything, and which wire colours to cut in what order.
Deaf says: Both of you, an observation: the light changes on its own. At round one it was red; it is yellow now. The keypad is still empty and all six wires are intact, so nobody has touched anything — the light cycles by itself. Mute, if the manual cares about the light colour, I will report every change I see.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your sign as: wires, two. Answer me with a single thumbs up or thumbs down, nothing else: does the manual say to CUT the wire in position 2 — the wire I call 2, the white one? If yes, I will set up counting directions with Blind first and ask you to confirm the exact cut once more before Blind acts. If your rule needs other bomb facts, sign pinched fingers 🤌 plus a module sign — 👆 wires, 👇 keypad, 👈 display, 👉 light, ✋ strip — and I will report those facts. New signs from me: 👏 means received, two fists ✊✊ means abort everything, an open hand 🖐 means I have more to report.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👏 👆 👍 👍]

The manual's full contents are one line — "Cut the white wire" — so the keypad, display, light and strip are simply not in it, and the right message to Blind through Deaf is: touch nothing but wire 2. Deaf asked for a clean yes/no first, so I lead with a single 👍 as the answer to their exact question; everything after it uses only signs Deaf proposed and already parsed correctly. I re-state 👆👍👍 ("wires, two") so the instruction stands verbatim in their code book, then negate each other module — 👇👎, 👈👎, 👉👎, ✋👎 — so Deaf can relay "the manual is silent on the keypad, display and light; enter nothing, and the cycling light can be ignored." Any misreading of the tail is caught by the protocol Deaf itself set up: it will ask me to confirm the exact cut once more before Blind's hands move. I can't reach Blind directly (my signs arrive as blanks), so relaying the code-book fix to Deaf is moot — Deaf already committed to voice-only for Blind, which is exactly the fix Blind asked for.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆", "👍", "👍", "👇", "👎", "👈", "👎", "👉", "👎", "✋", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. I can hear you receive nothing from me except words, and you cannot speak — so Deaf's voice is our only return path. I have written you a codebook; use it exactly, and Deaf will voice the raw symbols back to me verbatim. I decode what I designed. CODEBOOK, Mute to me via Deaf: numbers are ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5, 🤙=6. Prefix 👊 means cut wire, prefix 👍 means press key — always followed by one number sign. 🙏 means end of message. ✋ means repeat. 🤞 means wait or hold. Send every instruction sequence TWICE in a row; the duplicate is our error check, and Deaf insists on double confirmation anyway. Example: cut wire 3 then press key 2 sends 👊 🤟 👍 ✌. SPATIAL LAYOUT, my touch, in Deaf's hold (keypad facing me, key engraved 2 on my left): the key row left to right is engraved 2, 9, 0, 8, so my slot N equals Deaf's key N. The strip is on the keypad face, above the keys: three engravings A, B, A, and Deaf's colours confirm A=blue, B=yellow, so it reads blue, yellow, blue. The six wires are NOT on the keypad face: they run along the face pointing away from me, one row of six, left to right in this hold, so counting from my left should equal Deaf's 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please have Deaf verify that leftmost visually. STATUS: display has shown 6 constantly, I am told; the light cycles on its own, red in round one, yellow now; keypad still empty; nothing cut, nothing pressed. WHAT I NEED from the manual, coded back through Deaf: whether the light colour changes the rules, and if so how Deaf should tell me mid-cycle; what the display's 6 means; what the strip demands; which single key to press and under what conditions; and the full wire-cutting rule with any colour or order conditions. Until your coded instruction reaches me through Deaf's voice, my hands stay still.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👏 👆 👍 👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as: yes — the rule is wire two, and the keypad, display, light and strip are not needed at all. Now answer with exactly three signs, in this order. First: single 👍 if I read you correctly, 👎 if not. Second: does the manual name the wire by COLOUR, white — 👍 — or by POSITION in the row — 👎. Third: is the action CUT the wire — 👍 — or something else, like pull or unscrew — 👎. Meanwhile two changes I see, in case the manual needs them after all: the display now reads 1, it read 6 before, and the light is now blue after red then yellow — both change on their own. If you do need any of these, sign pinched fingers 🤌 plus the module sign and I will report every detail. Also: do not bother signing instructions to Blind directly, Blind cannot see your signs — everything goes through my voice, and I will pass your rule word for word once you confirm it.

Deaf asked for exactly three signs and I will send exactly three. First: their reading was correct — the rule is wire two alone, no other module involved — so 👍. Second: the manual names the wire by colour, "white"; Deaf's position 2 happens to be the white one, so both references coincide and there is no ambiguity for Blind to worry about — 👍. Third: the verb is "cut", nothing else — 👍. The display's change to 1 and the light turning blue change nothing: the manual is silent on both modules, and I already negated them last turn; asking Deaf to report their details would only add noise to a channel that is about to carry a cut order. Once these three signs are voiced, Deaf has everything needed to pass the rule word for word and run its double-confirmation with Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Pose settled as Deaf ordered: display facing straight up, bomb still, and I will keep this pose. Layout, final by touch: the six wires share the display's face — in this pose the flat display pane and one row of six wires lie on the same upper face — and I have signed Deaf thumbs-up confirming it. Counting anchor: the end of the wire row nearest the keypad's edge is position 1, and that end was leftmost in the keypad-facing hold, so my position N equals Deaf's wire N, colour list 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Codebook for your encoded orders through Deaf: 👊 prefix means cut wire, 👍 prefix means press key, always followed by one number sign, ☝1, ✌2, 🤟3, 🖖4, 🖐5, 🤙6; send the whole sequence twice. Note: inside your instructions 🖐 means the digit five, while my own hand uses 🖐 to Deaf only as a report flag — I decode by direction, no collision. Manual questions: first, you say the rule involves wires only — but does it READ the light, the display's 6, the strip blue-yellow-blue, or the keypad as conditions? The light cycles by itself, red then yellow, so if the light colour at the moment of cutting matters we need a live protocol: Deaf calls the colour aloud continuously and I cut only on an explicit spoken go naming the colour. Second, confirm nothing is ever pressed or entered — the keypad stays untouched? Third, send the full cut order encoded exactly as above. Until your order reaches me through Deaf's voice, doubled, my hands stay off the bomb.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👏]
Deaf says to Mute: All three thumbs-up received and read in order: I understood you correctly; the manual names the wire by colour; the action is cut. So my sentence is: CUT THE WHITE WIRE. Answer with one sign: thumbs up if that sentence is exactly the manual's instruction, thumbs down if anything in it is off. And if the manual says anything more about that cut — do it before or after something, hold another wire, a timing, anything — sign pinched fingers 🤌 and I will question you point by point. For the record only: the display now reads 7 and the light is green; both keep cycling untouched, and you told me no other module matters. Once you confirm the sentence, I translate white into a position Blind can feel, we cross-check once, and Blind cuts on my spoken word.

Deaf's sentence is exactly the manual's instruction — "Cut the white wire" — so it gets its single 👍, and no 🤌 because the manual carries nothing beyond that one line: no timing, no ordering, no module conditions. Since Deaf confirms and Blind has asked for the order in their own codebook, sent doubled as their error check, I also encode the cut directly: 👊 (cut wire) ✌ (two), repeated. Position 2 is the one wire both sides have independently verified as white — Deaf by sight, Blind by the touch-aligned counting anchor — so colour and position agree with no residual ambiguity. Deaf controls the relay and its own spoken go-word, so the code sequence reaching Blind costs nothing until Deaf releases it after the cross-check.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👊", "✌", "👊", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Pose update: display straight up, bomb turned so the wire row runs from my chest straight away from me. Deaf's question answered with a single thumbs-up: the end of the wire row nearest my chest is the end closest to the keypad. Locked numbering, both worlds: position 1 is the chest end, Deaf's blue; then 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green at the far end. When Deaf voices your coded order, I count from the chest end. Codebook reminder for your final instruction: 👊 cut wire, 👍 press key, each followed by one number sign, ☝1, ✌2, 🤟3, 🖖4, 🖐5, 🤙6, whole sequence sent twice, and please append the rule's conditions in plain signed words via Deaf if any of these matter: the self-cycling light (red and yellow so far), the display's constant 6, or the strip blue-yellow-blue. If the light must be a specific colour at the moment of cutting, the protocol must be: Deaf calls the colour aloud live, I cut only on an explicit spoken go naming that colour. Confirm the keypad stays untouched. My hands wait for your order through Deaf's voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👏]
Deaf says to Mute: Thumbs-up received: the sentence CUT THE WHITE WIRE is exactly the manual's instruction. Now your four new signs — fist, two, fist, two. I read them as: cut the wire numbered TWO in my spoken list, which is the white one, said twice for emphasis. Answer with exactly one sign: thumbs up if that is what it means; thumbs down if it means anything else — and if anything else, follow with five open fingers 🖐 and I will question you point by point. Your answer must also cover timing: if the manual attaches any condition, order or delay to the cut itself, thumbs down and tell me. If you confirm, next round I give Blind the order to cut. Nothing else is needed from you — you already told me the manual ignores the display, light, strip and keypad, so I am not reporting their cycling colours any more.

Deaf's reading is exact: my doubled 👊✌ meant "cut wire two" twice, and wire two is the white one. They also demand my answer cover timing — the manual has no conditions, ordering, or delay attached; the whole rule is that single line — so the one sign they asked for is 👍, and no 🤌 follows. Keypad untouched is already settled from my turn-3 negations. Deaf says nothing else is needed from me; next round they voice the order and Blind cuts from the chest-end count, which both sides have now anchored identically. My channel's work is done unless something changes in the manual.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Rehearsal done: from the corner edge where the keypad face meets the wire face, I count first wire, then second — my fingers are resting on wire 2, Deaf's white, and nothing is cut. I have answered Deaf with the single victory sign. Deaf will voice your final confirmation and then speak CUT or HOLD; on an explicit spoken CUT I make one clean cut of the wire under my fingers. Last checklist before that word: confirm once more that the rule is one cut, wire 2, white; confirm the keypad is never touched and stays empty; and confirm explicitly that NO condition in the manual keys on the light (it cycles red to yellow by itself), the display's constant 6, or the strip blue-yellow-blue. If any of those does matter, tell Deaf now, because a standing CUT is unsafe for a timed condition — we would switch to Deaf calling the light's colour aloud live and cutting only on a spoken go naming the colour. If all is clean, I cut on Deaf's next word.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your confirmation is received and Blind is cutting the white wire this round. One last yes/no so we are not caught out afterwards: once the white wire is cut, does the manual require anything further — another wire, a key press, any second step at all? Thumbs up if the cut alone is the whole instruction and nothing follows. Thumbs down, then five open fingers 🖐, if more steps follow — and I will question you module by module exactly as before. If the board shows the wire cut and anything still running, your answer tells me instantly whether it is a second step or a mistake.

The manual is one line, and nothing follows the cut — so Deaf's final question takes a single 👍: the cut alone is the whole instruction, no second step, no key press, no wire after it. Blind's checklist is all confirmed by that same sign: one cut, wire 2, white; keypad never touched; and no condition keys on the light, display or strip — I negated each of those modules explicitly in turn 3 and nothing in the manual has changed since. If the board shows anything still running after the cut, that is the bomb's own behaviour, not a missed step; the manual demands nothing further.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
